## January vs. February 2026 P&L — which month was stronger?

**February 2026 was stronger than January 2026**, primarily because **revenue increased by $130k (+5.3%) while OpEx rose only $11.5k (+0.8%)**, resulting in **EBITDA up $118.5k (+11.9%)** and a **~2.6 pp improvement in EBITDA margin** (calculations below based on the line items in the monthly P&Ls). [1][2]

### Headline comparison (actuals)
(All totals are **sums of the line items** shown in each month’s P&L.) [1][2]

| Metric | Jan 2026 | Feb 2026 | $ Change (Feb-Jan) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **Total Revenue** | **$2,470,000** | **$2,600,000** | **+$130,000** |
| **Total Operating Expenses (OpEx)** | **$1,474,300** | **$1,485,800** | **+$11,500** |
| **EBITDA (Revenue − OpEx)** | **$995,700** | **$1,114,200** | **+$118,500** |
| **EBITDA Margin** | **40.3%** | **42.9%** | **+2.6 pp** |

## What drove the difference?

### 1) Revenue was meaningfully higher in February (main driver)
February revenue outperformance vs January was driven mostly by **M&A Advisory Fees**:

- **M&A Advisory Fees:** $1,150,000 → $1,280,000 (**+ $130,000**) [1][2]  
- **Restructuring Advisory:** $720,000 → $680,000 (**− $40,000**) [1][2]  
- **Strategic Consulting:** $285,000 → $310,000 (**+ $25,000**) [1][2]  
- **Due Diligence Services:** $190,000 → $205,000 (**+ $15,000**) [1][2]  
- **Retainer Fees:** $125,000 → $125,000 (**flat**) [1][2]  

Net: **+$130,000 total revenue** (the M&A increase was the single biggest swing, partially offset by lower restructuring). [1][2]

### 2) Expenses were slightly higher in February, but not enough to offset revenue gains
Total OpEx increased **+$11,500** from January to February. The biggest MoM movements:

- **Travel & Entertainment:** $62,000 → $71,000 (**+ $9,000**) [1][2]  
- **Marketing & BD:** $28,000 → $32,000 (**+ $4,000**) [1][2]  
- **Technology & Software:** $38,000 → $39,500 (**+ $1,500**) [1][2]  
- **Miscellaneous:** $9,500 → $11,000 (**+ $1,500**) [1][2]  
Offset by:
- **Professional Development:** $15,000 → $12,000 (**− $3,000**) [1][2]  
- **Legal & Accounting:** $18,000 → $16,500 (**− $1,500**) [1][2]  

Most of the large fixed-cost lines (e.g., **Salaries & Wages $985,000**, **Office Lease $137,500**) were **flat MoM**, so the incremental revenue in February flowed through to EBITDA at a high rate. [1][2]

## Budget context (optional, but reinforces the conclusion)
- **January:** Revenue beat budget by **$95k** (2.470M vs 2.375M) while OpEx was **$19k over** budget (1.4743M vs 1.4553M). [1]  
- **February:** Revenue beat budget by **$225k** (2.600M vs 2.375M) while OpEx was **$30.5k over** budget (1.4858M vs 1.4553M). [2]  

So February was not only stronger vs January—it also delivered the larger top-line beat, more than compensating for somewhat higher variable spending. [1][2]
